أَعْقَدُ A wolf, (O, L, K,) and a dog, and a ram, and any other animal, (L.) having a twisted tail [as though it were tied in a knot]: (O, L, K:) and [the fem.] عَقْدَآءُ, a sheep or goat (شَاة) having a twisted tail as though it were knotted or tied in a knot. (S, * L, K. *) And الأَعْقَدُ signifies The dog; (S, O, L, K;) a well-known name thereof; (S, O, L;) because of his tail's being twisted as though it were tied in a knot. (S, L.) ―
-b2- And A crooked tail. (L.) ―
-b3- And A stallion [app. of the camels] that raises his tail; which he does by reason of sprightliness. (L.) ―
-b4- And A he-goat having a twist, or a knot, in his horn. (L.) ―
-b5- For one of its meanings as an epithet applied to a dog, see عُقْدَةٌ, latter half. ―
-b6- Also, and ↓ عَقِدٌ , A man having an impediment in his tongue; unable to speak freely; tongue-tied. (S, * O, * L, K. *) ―
-b7- And لَئِيمٌ أَعْقَدُ A mean man, of difficult, or stubborn, disposition. (ISk, O, L.) ―
-b8- And [the fem.] عَقْدَآءُ signifies A female slave. (AA, O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
